design: settle the surface as tearouts before building it

Prose about an interface cannot be judged. A paragraph describing a screen
can be reasonable and wrong at the same time, and nothing in it separates
the two.

These are real markup and real styling with fixture content, no backend and
no JavaScript, so look and interaction are settled in cheap static pages
rather than discovered halfway through building the real thing. Rendering
them found defects that reading the same markup had not: a passage marker
clipped out of existence inside a card, a link unreadable in one theme, a
phone layout stretched to a desktop column.

The checker covers what a browser will not complain about. An unstyled class
still renders text and a dead link still looks like a link, so each of those
failures arrives looking plausible.
